clue.text: Drink gallons at home

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for gallons
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Someone knocking back gallons of booze in their own house.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin is a juniper-flavoured spirit, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: One promising to hold the bride's train

definitions.text: One promising to hold the bride

blocks.clueFragment: One promising to hold the bride
blocks.note: first meaning: the man who vows at a wedding to have and to hold his bride
second meaning: the verb, to prepare or coach someone

explanation.surface: A wedding guest promising to carry the bride's long dress train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bride's train' reads as the trailing dress; in fact 's is 'is' and train is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridegroom makes wedding vows; to groom someone is to prepare or coach them for a role.

clue.text: Finite supply hampering old queen — with time she achieved great things

indicators.note: read as the adverb, supply means flexibly, so the word before bends into a new order
to hamper is to hem in, so the mixed letters enclose the queen

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A limited supply holding back an ancient queen, though in time she did great things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun meaning stock, but read as an adverb (supplely, pliantly) it signals the rearrangement. ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti, wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten, was a powerful Egyptian queen who helped drive a religious revolution.

clue.text: Misapplication of the French article in play is embodied by matriarch

indicators.note: something embodied by another is held inside its body, so the earlier words sit within the last

blocks.note: MAM, mother, the head of the family; it opens around the inner pieces
la is the feminine French definite article
a prop is an object used on stage in a play
taken as written
the closing letter of MAM, the other half of the container

explanation.surface: A grammarian complaining that a mother misuses the French article in a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: MAM (mother) holds LA + PROP + IS. Fittingly, the word comes from Mrs Malaprop, a character in Sheridan's play The Rivals, who misused words.
explanation.definitionFit: A malapropism is the mistaken use of a similar-sounding word, a misuse of vocabulary named after Sheridan's Mrs Malaprop.

clue.text: Madonna's first on, and the endless legendary content's belted out, eg Vogue

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the name before it
with no end, the word loses its final letter
with its contents thrown out only the word's two outside letters stay

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
taken as written
taken as written, before it loses its end
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Madonna performing her legendary hit Vogue at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Vogue is the Madonna song in the surface, but the definition means the fashion magazine, published once a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Vogue magazine is published every month, so it is an example of a periodical issued on that schedule.

clue.text: One embraced by fat landowner in Scotland

indicators.note: something embraced is held in the arms, so it sits inside the next word

blocks.note: lard is pig fat
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wealthy Scottish estate owner hugged by a fat man.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the owner of a large estate in Scotland, the Scots form of lord.

clue.text: Force folk to become sailors? Or journalists?

blocks.note: first meaning: the historic forced recruitment of men into the navy
second meaning, read literally: a gang of the press

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a mob is being drafted into the navy or into newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the verb (two words, press-gang); the second is a whimsical noun phrase, a crowd of reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval press-gangs seized men for service at sea; the press is journalism, and a gang is a group.

clue.text: East German aristocracy who won't face up to reality

definitions.text: who won't face up to reality
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who won't face up to reality'

blocks.note: Ost is the German word for east
the rich, the wealthy upper class

explanation.surface: Former East German nobility who refused to accept how things had changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the myth that the bird buries its head in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostrich is figuratively a person who ignores unpleasant facts, from the legend of the bird hiding its head in sand.

clue.text: Photograph in short periodical that is absorbing

indicators.note: to absorb is to take inside, so the preceding phrase holds the other piece

blocks.note: i.e., Latin id est, means that is
mag is short for magazine

explanation.surface: A photograph appearing in a brief, engrossing magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture, and a photograph is one kind of picture.

clue.text: Where are the brothers who won't speak to one another?

definitions.text: Where are the brothers who won't speak to one another?

blocks.clueFragment: Where are the brothers who won't speak to one another?
blocks.note: surface reading: a family feud, siblings not on speaking terms
setter's reading: monks under a vow of silence, and the place they live

explanation.surface: Someone asking where to find two estranged brothers who are not on speaking terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The brothers are not siblings who have fallen out but religious brothers keeping silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks are addressed as brothers, and many orders keep silence in the religious house where they live.

clue.text: Poor chicken's decapitated by Solomon's attack

blocks.note: food or a performance that is off is poor, below standard
hens are chickens
the setter Solomon refers to himself as I; 's stands for has, giving I've

explanation.surface: A sorry chicken has its head chopped off in an assault by Solomon.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for I, a common crossword convention, and 's here is 'has', making I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a military attack or campaign, so the noun matches 'attack'.

clue.text: Spinning tapestries, say, in school

blocks.note: tapestries are an example of art, as 'say' signals
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pupils learning to weave or spin tapestries at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun but is the verb, to educate or drill.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to instruct them, which is the verb sense of train.

clue.text: Did protest harm influential socialist democrat?

Che Guevara, the influential revolutionary socialist
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: Asking whether a protest damaged a prominent left-wing Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters who demonstrate walk in procession, so taking part in a demonstration is to have marched.

clue.text: Makers of silk dress fitted around Greek's figure

indicators.note: fitted suggests something altered to shape, so the letters of the word before are rearranged
around says the reworked letters go either side of the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
pi is the Greek letter used for the mathematical constant

explanation.surface: A silk dress tailored to fit a Greek woman's figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makers of silk' points at silkworms, but spiders spin silk too.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders produce silk threads from their spinnerets to build webs.

clue.text: How might one describe a bear? 'Dangerous'?

definitions.text: How might one describe a bear?

blocks.clueFragment: How might one describe a bear?
blocks.note: first meaning: covered in fur
second meaning: informal for risky or frightening

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether 'dangerous' is the right word for a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means shaggy with fur, and in slang a hairy situation is a perilous one.

clue.text: Inbred wrangler's latest daughter's wearing rawhide pants

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cowboy's daughter in leather trousers, with a hint of inbreeding on the ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers, which suits 'wearing' and 'rawhide', but here it is slang for rubbish. A wrangler is a cowboy who herds horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbred qualities are innate, built in from birth, which is the figurative sense of hard-wired.

clue.text: 9 agitated moles circling rats?

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 9 across, OFFENSIVE, in its adjective sense

circling means going all round, so the mixed letters surround the last piece

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
'Rats!' is an exclamation of annoyance, a mild oath or curse

explanation.surface: Nervous moles surrounding rats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rats' looks like animals beside the moles but is the exclamation, an OATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome is disgusting or repellent, the adjective sense of offensive.

clue.text: Piglets, perhaps, tip over part of pen and refuse to go in it

explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like the verb (the piglets won't go in), but it is the noun, rubbish; 'pen' is a writing pen, not a sty.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter bin is a public container where rubbish is put.

clue.text: Pit workers with lamps cycling the outer parts of Rhondda

the outer parts are the first and last letters of the next word

blocks.note: torches are portable lamps
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.walkthrough: The Rhondda mining picture makes 'Pit workers' coal miners; the pit is the orchestra pit below a stage. TORCHES with its T moved to the back gives ORCHEST.

clue.text: German seat and chairs get modified

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A German seat and some chairs being altered, as in a furniture workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' suggests furniture, alongside the chairs, but it is a seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag building in Berlin is where the German parliament sits, its seat of government.

clue.text: French king goes through bad weather to get pomade

blocks.note: hail is a kind of bad weather
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A French monarch braving a storm to buy hair cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented ointment for styling hair, an oily grooming product.

clue.text: Jammy woman snaffles the last piece of flapjack

indicators.note: the last piece is the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a woman's name
the final letter of the word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jammy' looks like part of the cake picture; it is British slang for fortunate.
explanation.definitionFit: Jammy is British slang meaning fortunate, as of someone who gets good breaks.

clue.text: Netting ling?

explanation.definitionFit: Hauling a caught fish out of the water is the angler's verb sense, so netting a fish is doing exactly that.

clue.text: Fake news and sex filling insignificant pages online

the last letter of WEE, closing the container

clue.text: Baby, there's no getting away from it — I'm cute

clue.text: At ease, in Tuscany, with camping equipment

the Roman numeral for one
the first letter of the word

clue.text: City close to archipelago that neighbours Quebec

clue.text: Part of regular circumference
